mirrordrive.notes:
# Mirror v0.15.0

### Features
- App renamed "Mirror" (from "MirrorDrive"/"Mirror Drive") in the launcher, app title, and app-store listing. Package id and OAuth client are unchanged, so this update installs normally over the existing app.
- Mapping backup now lives in Drive's hidden App Data folder, one file per device install, so the same Google account signed into two phones can no longer have one phone's auto-backup silently overwrite the other's saved mappings.
- A restore picker (Settings, or offered automatically right after a fresh sign-in with no local mappings) lists every device's backup under the account and lets you choose which one to restore.
- Mapping backup now saves automatically on every add/edit/delete, not just when manually tapping "Back up" in Settings.
- Optional fleet diagnostics reporting (Settings > Troubleshooting): sends sanitized failure and background-sync delivery signals to help diagnose device-specific issues remotely. Off by default; never sends mapping paths, file names, or account details.
- Removed the "beta" label from the app-store listing and the in-app sign-in screen.

### Bug fixes
- Google Sign-In on release builds no longer fails right after install (the v0.14.0 signing-key rotation needed its new SHA-1 registered on the OAuth client; done).
- Mapping backups now actually persist across an uninstall/reinstall. Previously the backup/restore mechanism existed but was never triggered automatically, so a reinstall lost every mapping.

family.notes:
﻿com.pnsjy.familylive · 67.9MB · release-signed · 213 tests
Also at **https://family.pnsjy.in/download/familylive.apk**

## The service could never start

The plugin does not declare its own foreground service — its manifest carries only the boot and restart receivers — so the app has to declare it, and this app never did. **From Android 14, starting a location foreground service without a matching `foregroundServiceType` declaration throws.**

That is almost certainly why the phone never reported while every screen said sharing was on: permissions granted, session live, service unable to start, and nothing anywhere saying so.

## What now covers the cases you listed

| Case | How |
| --- | --- |
| Phone locked, app in background | a foreground service is the only mechanism Android offers, and it can now start |
| App killed / swiped from recents | `stopWithTask="false"` — sharing survives a child tidying their task list |
| Phone restarted | auto-start on boot, which was already set and could not work while the service was undeclared |
| No signal | fixes queued on disk, uploaded in order when the network returns |

## You can now see whether it is actually working

The child's screen shows a card reading **"This phone is reporting"** or **"This phone is NOT reporting"**, read from the platform itself rather than the server. Every other signal came from the API, which can only say a session exists — it cannot know the service failed to start. That gap is what left a family believing a phone was tracked when it was not.

## How to verify, in order
1. Install on the child's phone, sign in, complete the permission gate — **including the battery exemption**.
2. Check the child screen says **"This phone is reporting"**. If it does not, nothing else will work.
3. Lock the phone, wait two minutes, look at the parent's map.
4. Swipe the app out of recents, wait two minutes, look again.
5. Restart the phone, wait a few minutes, look again.

Step 2 is the one that used to fail silently.

## Not in this build
Check-in, push notifications (skipped for now — alerts only show with the app open), iOS, and the backend still runs on the laptop.

taashclub.notes:
Taash Club 1.1.0 - Playable 3-2-5 vs Computer, and Rules You Can Argue With

### Features
- Rules page for every game, reached from the game card in the lobby. Teen Patti, Rummy and 3-2-5 each get their deal, their rankings or contracts, and the house rules a table can vary.
- Feedback on any individual rule. If a rule is wrong, unclear, or simply not how your family plays, say so on that rule itself. Notes written offline are kept on the device and sent when you are next online, so a disagreement at the table is never lost.
- Solo play against the computer now works for Teen Do Paanch (3-2-5): kaat is called, all ten tricks are played out, and the deal is settled against the 3-2-5 contracts.
- Solo play against the computer now works for Rummy: draw from either pile, discard, drop, and declare, with the computer players drawing, discarding and declaring for themselves. If the cards run out before anyone declares, the deal is settled on the lowest count.

### Bug fixes
- Fixed 3-2-5 against the computer freezing immediately after the deal. The table appeared, cards were visible, and nothing further happened: the opening turn belonged to a computer player that was never asked to move.
- Fixed Rummy against the computer dealing a hand and then ignoring every tap. Drawing, discarding, dropping and declaring all did nothing, because only Teen Patti had an offline engine behind it.
- Fixed the 3-2-5 deck keeping one red and one black seven regardless of the table's house rule. It now keeps the pair the table actually chose, matching the server.
- Fixed the 3-2-5 setting for sevens describing the opposite of what it does. "Keep the black sevens" in fact removed them; the option now names what is removed and which pair is left in play.
- Fixed Teen Patti wild-card hands being scored differently depending on the order the cards were dealt. An Ace-low run built with a wild could be read as a pair, so the same three cards could win or lose.

### Notes for existing players
- This release is signed with a new key. Android will not install it over version 1.0.1, so uninstall the old app first and then install this one. Chips, profile and history live on the server and are restored when you sign in again.
